title: Fecal Indicator Bacteria
text: Fecal Indicator Bacteria (FIB) used track concentrations pathogens surface waters may detrimental human health environment. Exposure risk commonly measured select indicators present human gut can enter environment wastewater discharges, stormwater, illicit sources. Common indicators include concentrations E. coli, Enterococcus, Fecal Coliform number colony forming units (CFU) per 100 mL water. Many monitoring programs routinely measure FIB concentrations select locations. tbeptools package several functions importing reporting data. Three workflows available: Functions use data exclusively Environmental Protection Commission (EPC) Hillsborough County Functions use data Manatee, Pasco, Polk, Hillsborough (Environmental Services Division) Counties Functions use data several monitoring programs baywide reporting focusing exclusively Enterococcus vignette organized around three workflows. , assessments meant inform progress remediating fecal impairments support prioritization areas investigation. meant support beach monitoring efforts closures recreational uses - alternative reporting products available purpose (see FLDOH Healthy Beaches Tampa Bay Recreational Water Quality Map).

text: rest seagrass functions tbeptools developed work complete database. show_complot() function (see ) developed training data. rest functions can used estimate plot frequency occurrence data. anlz_transectocc() function summarizes frequency occurrence transects dates collapsing species results across quadrats within transect. Abundance frequency occurrence estimated Sherwood et al. 2017, equations 1 2 [1]. short, frequency occurrence estimated number instances species observed along transect divided number placements along transect average abundance estimated sum species-specific Braun-Blanquet scores divided number placements along transect. estimates obtained seagrass species, including Caulerpa spp. (attached macroalgae), Dapis (cyanobacteria), Chaetomorpha (drift green algae), whereas attached drift algae species aggregated. Drift attached macroalgae cyanobacteria (Dapis) estimates may accurate prior 2021. second function, anlz_transectave(), takes results anlz_transectocc() estimates annual results across major bay segments seagrass species averaging frequency occurrence across transects. function used internally within show_transectmatrix() function create summary plots. frequency occurrence estimates also binned categories simple trend assessments, e.g., red < 25%, orange 25-50%, yellow 50-75%, green > 75%. Results specific bay segments annual ranges can filtered bay_segment yrrng arguments. third function, anlz_transectavespp(), takes results anlz_transectocc() estimates annual averages across major bay segments last function, results retained individual species. function used internally within show_transectavespp() function create summary plots. summaries aggregated across selected bay segments, .e., default average species/year across segments. Results individual bay segment can returned appropriate argument, e.g., using bay_segment = 'OTB' select Old Tampa Bay. Results can also filtered specific species using species argument, default return . Caulerpa spp., Dapis spp., Chaetomorpha spp. also included. Results individual bay segments anlz_transectavespp() can retained setting by_seg argument TRUE. Note totals returned case.

title: Tampa Bay Benthic Index
text: Tampa Bay Benthic Index (TBBI) [1,2]) assessment method quantifies ecological health benthic community Tampa Bay. index provides complementary approach evaluating environmental condition supported assessment methods currently available region (e.g., water quality report card, nekton index, etc.). tbeptools package includes several functions described import data required index plot results view trends time. functions described detail . TBBI uses data Tampa Bay Benthic Monitoring Program part Environmental Protection Commission (EPC) Hillsborough Country. data updated annually public site maintained EPC, typically December Summer/Fall sampling. website hosts water quality data used water quality report card. required data TBBI extensive water quality report card data made available zipped folder csv files, available . process downloading working data similar functions tbeptools.

title: Tampa Bay Benthic Index
text: AZTI Marine Biotic Index (AMBI) measure benthic community health based pollution sensitivity organisms found sampling station. Benthic macroinvertebrates assigned one five ecological groups ranging Group (sensitive, typical clean conditions) Group V (tolerant, typical heavily disturbed conditions) based established taxonomic lists [3]. Biotic Coefficient (BC) calculated weighted sum proportion taxa records group: BC=0×%G1+1.5×%G2+3×%G3+4.5×%G4+6×%G5100BC = \frac{0 \times \%G1 + 1.5 \times \%G2 + 3 \times \%G3 + 4.5 \times \%G4 + 6 \times \%G5}{100} Lower BC values indicate undisturbed conditions dominated sensitive species, higher values (approaching 7) indicate heavily stressed communities. Azoic stations (empty samples organisms) receive BC 7. adjusted score 0 10 scale also computed (7−BC)×10/7(7 - BC) \times 10/7, higher values indicate healthier conditions. Pollution categories assigned based adjusted score: Unpolluted (8.29), Slightly Polluted (5.29 8.29), Meanly Polluted (2.89 5.29), Heavily Polluted (1.39 2.89), Extremely Polluted (1.39). Azoic stations assigned adjusted score zero treated Extremely Polluted. tbeptools package supports two AMBI variants calculated benthicdata object used TBBI. standard variant uses Gulf Mexico ecological group assignments [3], Tampa Bay-specific variant (AMBI-TB) uses group assignments tailored local benthic community [1]. variants use scoring formula, taxon--group mapping differs.

title: Get AMBI scores for benthic stations — anlz_ambiscr
text: function calculates AZTI Marine Biotic Index (AMBI) benthic stations Tampa Bay.  index assigns taxon one five ecological groups (= sensitive, V = tolerant pollution) computes Biotic Coefficient (BC) proportion taxa group. Biotic Coefficient calculated : $$BC = (0 \times \%G1 + 1.5 \times \%G2 + 3 \times \%G3 + 4.5 \times \%G4 + 6 \times \%G5) / 100$$ \ adjusted AMBI score 0-10 scale also returned: $$Adjusted AMBI = (7 - BC) \times (10 / 7)$$ Higher adjusted scores indicate healthier benthic conditions.  Azoic stations (empty samples, TaxaListID == 1942 benthicdata) receive BC = 7 adjusted score = 0. Two variants supported via type argument.  "AMBI" uses ecological group assignments published literature (AMBIGroupID ambispp).  "AMBI-TB" uses Tampa Bay-specific assignments (TBAMBIGroupID ambispp).  calculation identical, group assignment column differs.

title: Analyze Fecal Indicator Bacteria categories over time by station or bay segment — anlz_fibmatrix
text: function used create output plotting matrix stoplight graphic FIB categories station. station (bay segment) year combination categorized based likelihood fecal indicator bacteria concentrations exceeding threshold given year.  Enterococcus (marine), default threshold 130 CFU / 100 mL given year.  E. coli (fresh), default threshold 410 CFU / 100 mL.  proportions categorized , B, C, D, E (Microbial Water Quality Assessment MWQA categories) corresponding colors, breakpoints category <10\ input data read_importentero (baywide assessment), results can summarized bay segment bay_segment NULL. stas argument ignored stations within bay segment watershed used evaluate FIB categories. yrrng can specified several ways.  yrrng = NULL, year range data selected changes chosen.  User-defined values minimum maximum years can also used, minimum maximum can specified, e.g., yrrng = c(2000, 2010) yrrng = c(2000, NA).  latter case, maximum year defined data. default stations input read_importfib (EPC data) bay_segment NULL used TBEP report #05-13 (https://drive.google.com/file/d/1MZnK3cMzV7LRg6dTbCKX8AOZU0GNurJJ/view) Hillsborough River Basin Management Action Plan (BMAP) subbasins.  include Blackwater Creek (WBID 1482, EPC stations 143, 108), Baker Creek (WBID 1522C, EPC station 107), Lake Thonotosassa (WBID 1522B, EPC stations 135, 118), Flint Creek (WBID 1522A, EPC station 148), Lower Hillsborough River (WBID 1443E, EPC stations 105, 152, 137).  stations can plotted using stas argument. Input read_importwqp Manatee County (21FLMANA_WQX), Pasco County (21FLPASC_WQX), Polk County (21FLPOLK_WQX) FIB data can also used.  function tested organizations.

title: Import PRISM daily weather data — read_importprism
text: vars character vector PRISM variables download crop. default c("tmin", "tmax", "tdmean", "ppt"). See Details . vars_ytd character vector PRISM variables summed year date, gets recorded new layer suffix "ytd". default precipitation c("ppt"), layer "pptytd" gets added PRISM daily rasters. date_beg defaults start PRISM daily availability 1981-01-01. date_end defaults today's date, adjusted recently available data, per update schedule. CAUTION: try request date-variable given day, get error PRISM service message like "tried download file PRISM_tdmean_stable_4kmD2_19810101_bil.zip twice one day (Pacific local time).  Note repeated offenses may result IP address blocked." bbox bounding box spatial extent crop PRISM daily rasters, bigger st_bbox(sf_zones). dir_tif directory path store downloaded cropped PRISM daily rasters (GeoTIFF) across years file name format prism_daily_{month}-{day}.tif. default path sub("\\.[^.]*$", "", zonal_csv).  Date version raster layers compared update schedule determine updated, otherwise skipped. pfx_tif prefix PRISM daily raster files, appended month-day. Defaults "prism_daily_". sf_zones spatial feature object (sf) zones extract zonal statistics PRISM daily weather data fld_zones character vector unique field name(s) sf_zones include extracted zonal statistics zonal_fun function apply terra::zonal() function. Defaults "mean". options "min", "max", "sum", "isNA", "notNA". zonal_csv path output zonal statistics (terra::zonal()) table CSV format redo_zonal logical whether recalculate zonal statistics. text: function retrieves data Water Quality Portal API (https://www.waterqualitydata.us/) selected counties around Tampa Bay watershed. type data returned defined type argument either "wq" "fib" water quality Fecal Indicator Bacteria data, respectively. org argument retrieves data specific organization. Valid entries org include "21FLCOSP_WQX" (City St. Petersburg), "21FLDOH_WQX" (Florida Department Health), "21FLHILL_WQX" (Hillsborough County), "21FLMANA_WQX" (Manatee County), "21FLPASC_WQX" (Pasco County), "21FLPDEM_WQX" (Pinellas County), "21FLPOLK_WQX" (Polk County), "21FLTPA_WQX" (Florida Department Environmental Protection, Southwest District), "21FLHESD_WQX" (Hillsborough County Environmental Services Division).  naming convention follows Organization ID Water Quality Portal. function fetches results station metadata, combines formats using read_formwqp function, returns processed data data frame.  Parameters specific type argument. Requests retried exponential backoff (via util_importwqp) max_retries times Water Quality Portal API returns intermittent failure.

title: Format a Vector of Years into a Concise Range — util_frmyrrng
text: Takes vector years formats concise string representation. consecutive years within century, end year shortened (e.g., "2010-14"). years spanning different centuries non-consecutive years, full years used (e.g., "1998-2001"). Optional prefix suffix can added formatted range.

title: Format a Vector of Years into a Concise Range — util_frmyrrng
code: util_frmyrrng(years, prefix = "", suffix = "")

title: Format a Vector of Years into a Concise Range — util_frmyrrng
text: years Numeric vector years (integers). Can single year multiple years. prefix Character string prepend formatted range. Default empty string. suffix Character string append formatted range. Default empty string.

title: Format a Vector of Years into a Concise Range — util_frmyrrng
text: character string representing year range concise format, optional prefix suffix. Returns empty character vector input NULL empty.

title: Format a Vector of Years into a Concise Range — util_frmyrrng
code: # Basic usage util_frmyrrng(2023)  # Returns "2023" #> [1] "2023" util_frmyrrng(2020:2024)  # Returns "2020-24" #> [1] "2020-24"  # Using prefix and suffix util_frmyrrng(2023, prefix = "FY ")  # Returns "FY 2023" #> [1] "FY 2023" util_frmyrrng(2020:2024, suffix = " AD")  # Returns "2020-24 AD" #> [1] "2020-24 AD" util_frmyrrng(2020:2024, prefix = "Years ", suffix = " CE")  # Returns "Years 2020-24 CE" #> [1] "Years 2020-24 CE"  # Other examples util_frmyrrng(1998:2001)  # Returns "1998-2001" #> [1] "1998-2001" util_frmyrrng(c(2020, 2022))  # Returns "2020-2022" #> [1] "2020-2022" util_frmyrrng(c(2010, 2011, 2012), prefix = "c. ")  # Returns "c. 2010-12" #> [1] "c. 2010-12"  # Empty input util_frmyrrng(numeric(0))  # Returns character(0) #> character(0)
